audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-025): Log topics tuple MUST have at most 4 elements
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Log construction (LOG0-LOG4 opcodes, topics validation) is an execution layer concern. Prysm is a consensus layer client that only receives LogsBloom as an opaque 256-byte array in the ExecutionPayload header via Engine API. Prysm does not construct logs, validate log topics, or execute EVM opcodes.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-029): Receipt data structure MUST be immutable after construction
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Receipt construction and immutability enforcement are execution layer concerns. Prysm only receives ReceiptsRoot as a 32-byte hash in the ExecutionPayload header. Prysm does not construct, store, or mutate Receipt objects.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-023): cumulative_gas_used field in Receipt MUST be monotonically non-decreasing
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). The cumulative_gas_used field in Receipt is an execution layer data structure. Prysm only receives ReceiptsRoot as a 32-byte hash in ExecutionPayload. Prysm does not process individual receipts or validate cumulative gas ordering.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: bloom filter in Receipt MUST be consistent with logs
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Bloom filter consistency with receipt logs is an execution layer concern. Prysm receives LogsBloom as an opaque 256-byte field in ExecutionPayload and ReceiptsRoot as a 32-byte hash. It does not compute or verify bloom-to-log consistency.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: bloom bytearray MUST be exactly 256 bytes (2048 bits)
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). The add_to_bloom function and bloom filter byte-length invariant are execution layer concepts. Prysm's ExecutionPayload SSZ schema enforces LogsBloom as a fixed 256-byte field via SSZ encoding (ssz-size:"256"), but this is a transport format constraint, not the EL bloom construction logic under test.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: In add_to_bloom, bit_to_set value MUST be in range [0, 2047]
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). The add_to_bloom function with bit_to_set computation and 0x07FF masking is an execution layer implementation. Prysm does not implement bloom filter construction or the add_to_bloom algorithm.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: In add_to_bloom, byte_index MUST be in range [0, 255]
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). The add_to_bloom byte_index computation is an execution layer implementation. Prysm does not implement bloom filter construction or byte-level bloom operations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the GAS_CAP constant exactly 16777216 (2^24) in all code paths?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). The per-transaction GAS_CAP of 16777216 is an execution layer concept enforced in EL txpool and block validation. Prysm is a consensus layer client. No GAS_CAP or per-tx gas cap constant exists in the Prysm codebase. The value 16777216 only appears in SSZ HistoricalRoots list max-length bounds, unrelated to per-tx gas.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does txpool reject transactions with gasLimit > 16777216?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Transaction pool (txpool) is an execution layer component. Prysm does not have a txpool and does not validate individual transaction gas limits. The only txpool reference in Prysm is in test harness code that spawns geth (an EL client).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does P2P-relayed transaction validation match local validation?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). P2P transaction relay and per-transaction validation are execution layer concerns. Prysm's P2P layer handles beacon blocks, attestations, and blobs — not individual EL transactions. Transaction validation convergence between P2P and local paths is purely an EL concern.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation reject blocks containing over-cap transactions?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Per-transaction gas cap validation within blocks is an execution layer concern. Prysm delegates execution payload validation to the EL via Engine API (engine_newPayloadV*). Prysm does not inspect individual transactions within the execution payload.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation check ALL transactions without skipping?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Transaction-level validation within blocks (iteration over all transactions, no early exit) is an execution layer concern. Prysm passes the entire execution payload to the EL via Engine API for validation. It does not iterate or validate individual transactions.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the entire block rejected when any transaction violates gas cap?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Atomic block rejection based on individual transaction gas cap violations is an execution layer concern. Prysm receives a binary valid/invalid response from the EL via Engine API. It does not implement transaction-level gas cap checking.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is per-transaction gas cap independent of block gas limit?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). The distinction between per-transaction gas cap and block gas limit is an execution layer enforcement concern. Prysm only handles block-level GasLimit in the ExecutionPayload header for the block gas limit adjustment algorithm (expectedGasLimit), not per-transaction caps.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are both txpool and block validation independently enforcing the gas cap?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Defense-in-depth validation at both txpool and block validation layers is an execution layer concern. Prysm does not have a txpool or per-transaction block validation. It delegates all execution payload validation to the EL via Engine API.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the gas cap value 16777216 identical at both enforcement points?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Constant consistency between txpool and block validation enforcement points is an execution layer concern. Prysm does not define or reference a per-transaction gas cap constant of 16777216.

audit_items.title: Is a rejected transaction dropped and never forwarded to block building?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Transaction rejection and block building queue isolation are execution layer concerns. Prysm does not manage a transaction pool or transaction lifecycle. Block building is delegated to the EL via Engine API (engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV*).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the comparison operator <= (not <) used for gas cap check?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). The comparison operator used for per-transaction gas cap enforcement is an execution layer implementation detail. Prysm does not implement per-transaction gas cap comparison logic.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do all clients use identical comparison semantics (> not >=)?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Cross-client comparison semantics for per-transaction gas cap is an execution layer concern. Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not enforce per-transaction gas caps. This check requires auditing EL clients (geth, nethermind, besu, erigon).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding of gasLimit strictly validated across all clients?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). RLP encoding validation of transaction gasLimit is an execution layer concern. Prysm uses SSZ encoding for consensus objects, not RLP. Transaction-level RLP parsing occurs in EL clients.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is per-tx cap enforced even when block gas limit exceeds it?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Per-transaction gas cap enforcement independent of block gas limit is an execution layer concern. Prysm only handles block-level gas limit in the ExecutionPayload header.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas cap validation O(1) per transaction with minimal memory?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Per-transaction gas cap validation complexity is an execution layer concern. Prysm does not perform per-transaction gas cap validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation catch over-cap transactions from direct block construction?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Block validation catching over-cap transactions from Engine API / MEV builder paths is an execution layer concern. Prysm delegates payload validation to the EL. It does not inspect individual transaction gas limits in execution payloads.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does transaction replacement re-validate gasLimit?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Transaction replacement (same nonce, higher fee) and re-validation of gasLimit is an execution layer txpool concern. Prysm does not manage transaction replacement or a txpool.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gasLimit covered by the transaction signature?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL). Transaction signature coverage of gasLimit is an execution layer concern governed by EIP transaction type specifications. Prysm does not sign, verify, or parse individual EL transactions. It handles consensus-layer signatures (BLS) on beacon blocks.
